Edwin McMillan is a physicist. McMillan co-invented the synchrotron with Vladimir Veksler, and after the war he returned to the Berkeley Radiation Laboratory to build them.
Who among these is a chemist?
Henry Taube is a chemist. Taube completed his undergraduate and master's degrees at the University of Saskatchewan, and his PhD from the University of California, Berkeley.
What is the atomic number of Sodium?
Sodium is a chemical element; it has symbol Na (from Neo-Latin natrium) and atomic number 11.
In what year was Javier Milei born?
Javier Milei: Javier Gerardo Milei (born 22 October 1970) is an Argentine politician and economist who has served as the 57th president of Argentina since 2023.
In what year was HIV/AIDS discovered?
HIV/AIDS: The human immunodeficiency virus (HIV) is a retrovirus that attacks the immune system.
In what year was COVID-19 discovered?
COVID-19: Coronavirus disease 2019 (COVID-19) is a contagious disease caused by the coronavirus SARS-CoV-2.
Mannitol: Pfizer. Mannitol is a type of sugar alcohol used as a sweetener and medication.
In which country did the Junkers Ju 87 take place?
Junkers Ju 87: Germany. The Junkers Ju 87, popularly known as the "Stuka", is a German dive bomber and ground-attack aircraft.
Who is credited with discovering Tellurium?
Tellurium: Franz-Joseph Müller von Reichenstein. Tellurium is a chemical element; it has the symbol Te and atomic number 52.
Who is credited with discovering Einsteinium?
Einsteinium: Albert Ghiorso. Einsteinium is a synthetic chemical element; it has symbol Es and atomic number 99 and is a member of the actinide series and the seventh transuranium element.
Who is credited with discovering Neon?
Neon: William Ramsay. Neon is a chemical element; it has the symbol Ne and the atomic number 10.
Affecting about 1 in 30,000 newborns, this inherited condition — also called rod monochromacy — brings color blindness, poor acuity, and a curious day-blindness. What is it?
Achromatopsia is a medical syndrome that exhibits symptoms relating to five conditions, most notably monochromacy.
This amphoteric compound forms a gelatinous precipitate in water and occurs naturally as the mineral gibbsite, one of bauxite's key components — what is it?
Aluminium hydroxide is a white chemical compound that is found as the mineral gibbsite (also known as hydrargillite) and its three much rarer polymorphs: bayerite, doyleite, and nordstrandite.
It can't touch a virus or a fungus, but a few varieties even fight protozoa — this class of drug is the frontline weapon against bacterial infection; what is it?
Antibiotic is a type of antimicrobial substance active against bacteria.

This lung condition — the partial collapse of alveoli that reduces gas exchange, usually in just one lung — is a very common finding on chest X-rays, though it's technically distinct from a fluid-filled lung or a full pneumothorax — what is it?
Atelectasis is the partial collapse or closure of a lung resulting in reduced or absent gas exchange, more specifically the collapse of alveoli.
This steroid medication treats conditions ranging from rheumatoid arthritis and psoriasis to asthma, and is also given before preterm birth to help speed a baby's lung development — what drug is it?
Betamethasone is a steroid medication. It can be taken by mouth, injected into a muscle, or applied to the skin, typically in cream, lotion, or liquid forms.
First described in 1903 from fossils found in Colorado, this sauropod dinosaur's Greek name means arm lizard, a reference to its proportionately long front limbs — what genus is it?
Brachiosaurus is a genus of sauropod dinosaur that lived in North America during the Late Jurassic, about 155.6 to 145.5 million years ago.
This group of diseases involves uncontrolled cell growth, includes over 100 types, and is responsible for about 33% of deaths when linked to tobacco and alcohol. What disease are we discussing?
Cancer is a group of diseases involving uncontrolled cell growth typically resulting in tumors with the potential to invade or spread to other parts of the body.
A biochemist hailed as the father of industrial fermentation, he was also instrumental in securing the 1917 Balfour Declaration before becoming the first president of Israel — who was he?

Chaim Weizmann (KYME; 27 November 1874 - 9 November 1952) was an Israeli statesman, biochemist, and Zionist leader who served as president of the Zionist Organization and later as the first president of Israel.
Once home to a bacterium behind a common cause of diarrhea before its 2016 reclassification, this genus of soil-dwelling bacteria also causes botulism — which genus?
Clostridium is a genus of anaerobic, Gram-positive bacteria.
What's the statistical term for the extent to which two variables are linearly related — famously not the same thing as causation?
Correlation is a type of statistical relationship between two random variables or bivariate data.
Known mostly through DNA evidence rather than abundant fossils, this extinct group of archaic humans ranged across Asia between roughly 200,000 and 32,000 years ago — what are they called?
Denisovan (d-(nz)) are an extinct species or subspecies of archaic human that ranged across Asia during the Middle to Late Pleistocene, approximately 200,000-32,000 years ago.
Sometimes called word blindness, this learning disability makes reading, writing, or speaking difficult despite a normal desire to learn, and often overlaps with ADHD — name the condition?
Dyslexia is a learning disability that affects either reading, writing, or speaking.
This tightly coiled duct sits behind each testicle, serving as the crucial link to the vas deferens where sperm mature before their onward journey — what is it?
Epididymis (pl.: epididymides or) is an elongated tubular genital organ attached to the posterior side of each one of the two male reproductive glands, the testicles.

Discovered in the debris of the first hydrogen bomb in 1952 and named for a pioneer of nuclear physics, element 100 is the heaviest that neutron bombardment can produce. Which synthetic element is it?
Fermium is a synthetic chemical element; it has symbol Fm and atomic number 100.

Lasting anywhere from milliseconds to hours, these are the most luminous explosions in the universe after the Big Bang, sometimes triggered when massive stars collapse into black holes — what are they?
Gamma-ray burst (GRBs) are extremely energetic events occurring in distant galaxies that represent the brightest and most powerful class of explosion in the Universe.

This American computer scientist and Navy rear admiral devised the theory of machine-independent programming languages and used it to help create COBOL, after being one of the first programmers on the Harvard Mark I — who is she?
Grace Hopper (ne Murray; December 9, 1906 - January 1, 1992) was an American computer scientist, mathematician, and United States Navy rear admiral.

Producer of Japan's first major turn-based role-playing video game, this Dutch-born American entrepreneur also secured console distribution rights to a Russian puzzle game and resolved the licensing disputes that brought it to the Game Boy — who is he?
Henk Rogers is a Dutch-born American video game designer and entrepreneur.
Often confused with a benign tumor, this cell-proliferation process increases an organ's cell count rather than the size of each cell — which term?

Hyperplasia (from Ancient Greek (hupr) 'over' and (plsis) 'formation'), or hypergenesis, is an enlargement of an organ or tissue caused by an increase in the amount of tissue that results from cell proliferation.
Whose 1687 book Principia Mathematica achieved the first great unification in physics and established classical mechanics?

Nicknamed 'Marvellous Merchiston,' this Scottish laird and mathematician popularised the decimal point and invented a set of calculating 'bones' — but he's best known for discovering what underlies the slide rule. Who was he?
John Napier (Latinized as Ioannes Neper; 1 February 1550 - 4 April 1617), nicknamed Marvellous Merchiston, was a Scottish landowner known as a mathematician, physicist and astronomer.

Named after a French mathematician but reportedly learned from his Swiss tutor, this calculus theorem evaluates tricky limits by taking derivatives of the numerator and denominator — what is it called?
L'Hôpital's rule (loh-pee-TAHL) is a mathematical theorem used for evaluating the limit of a quotient of two functions, each of which tends to zero or infinity, by taking each function's derivative.
Serving as a somatosensory organ as well as a tool for eating and forming sounds, this pair of soft facial features is one of the most visible parts of the mouth — what are they?
Lip are a horizontal pair of soft appendages attached to the jaws and are the most visible part of the mouth of many animals, including humans.
Roughly 60% the diameter of Pluto and stained reddish-brown by tholins, this trans-Neptunian dwarf planet carries minor-planet number 136472 — what is it?
Makemake (minor-planet number 136472) is a dwarf planet orbiting the Sun in the Kuiper belt, a disc of icy bodies beyond the orbit of Neptune.
This genus of about 20 species in the Lamiaceae family readily hybridizes where different species' ranges overlap, and thrives best in wet, moist soils — what genus is it?
Mentha (from Greek mntha, Linear B mi-ta), is a genus of flowering plants in the mint family, Lamiaceae.
A small terrestrial carnivore of the family Herpestidae that feasts mainly on insects, reptiles, and birds — and turns up as an introduced pest in Hawaii — what creature is it?
Mongoose is a small terrestrial carnivorous mammal belonging to the family Herpestidae.
A naval aviator who flew the F9F Panther in Korea before commanding Apollo 11, this Ohio-born engineer earned a place in history in 1969 — who is he?
Neil Armstrong (August 5, 1930 - August 25, 2012) was an American astronaut and aeronautical engineer who, as the commander of the 1969 Apollo 11 mission, became the first person to walk on the Moon.

Encompassing 24 genera from baboons to colobus to langurs, this is the largest primate family, having diverged from a separate primate lineage 45 to 55 million years ago before apes split off from it too — which family?
Old World monkey are primates in the family Cercopithecidae.
Making up the order Psittaciformes, these birds are known for a strong curved beak, upright stance, and clawed feet, with a third of all species threatened by extinction — name the group?
Parrot (order Psittaciformes), also known as psittacines from the name of the type genus Psittacus, are birds with a strong curved beak, upright stance, and clawed feet.
One of nine essential amino acids we must eat rather than make ourselves, it's found in mammals' milk and acts as a direct precursor to the neuromodulator phenethylamine — which molecule is it?
Phenylalanine (symbol Phe or F) is an -amino acid with the formula C9H11NO2.

This natural process transfers pollen from a flower's anther to its stigma, enabling fertilization and seed production, carried out by everything from bees and bats to wind and water — what process is it?
Pollination is the transfer of pollen from an anther of a plant to the stigma of a plant, later enabling fertilisation and the production of seeds.

This medical specialty diagnoses, treats, and prevents disorders of cognition, perception, mood, emotion, and behavior, typically beginning assessment with a case history and mental status exam — name the field?
Psychiatry is the medical specialty devoted to the diagnosis, treatment, and prevention of deleterious mental conditions.
One of the three ancient arts of discourse alongside grammar and logic, this discipline studies the techniques speakers and writers use to inform, persuade, and motivate an audience — what is it?
Rhetoric is the art of persuasion.
Which plant genus in the mint family, comprising nearly 1,000 species of shrubs and perennials, includes both a common cooking herb and — surprisingly — rosemary as one of its species?
Salvia is the largest genus of plants in the sage family Lamiaceae, with just under 1,000 species of shrubs, herbaceous perennials, and annuals.
Until 2010, this pungent little cultivar of the onion was classified as its own species before being folded back into the common onion — name this allium?
Shallot is a cultivar group of the onion. Until 2010, the (French red) shallot was classified as a separate species, Allium ascalonicum.
This family of roughly 1,450 moth species, with narrow wings and streamlined bodies built for fast, hovering flight, are so nimble they're routinely mistaken for hummingbirds — what are they called?
Sphingidae are a family of moths commonly called sphinx moths, also colloquially known as hawk moths, with many of their caterpillars known as hornworms.
These large waterfowl of the genus Cygnus are close relatives of geese and ducks, and are known for typically mating for life. What birds are they?
Swan are birds of the genus Cygnus within the family Anatidae.
Raised in Michigan with little schooling, he sold his first inventions by age 22 and moved to New York to chase engineering — going on to become one of America's most famous inventors. Who?
Thomas Edison (February 11, 1847 - October 18, 1931) was an American inventor and businessman.
Native to Central and South America but now found in sub-Saharan Africa, which parasitic flea burrows into skin to cause the condition tungiasis?
Tunga penetrans is a species of flea also known as the jigger, jigger flea, chigoe, chigo, chigoe flea, chigo flea, nigua, sand flea, or burrowing flea.

This forceful expulsion of stomach contents through the mouth can result from food poisoning, pregnancy, motion sickness, or more serious causes like brain tumors, and is usually preceded by nausea — name this bodily reaction?
Vomiting (scientifically known as emesis, and otherwise known as puking, and throwing up) is the forceful expulsion of the contents of one's stomach through the mouth and sometimes the nose.

This Indian Islamic preacher and comparative-religion scholar delivers his speeches in English while wearing a suit and tie, and founded both a research foundation and a television channel called Peace TV — who is he?
Zakir Naik (born 18 October 1965) is an Indian Islamic da'i and orator who focuses on comparative religion.
Prescribed for ADHD and narcolepsy but also misused as a euphoriant, this fixed-dose pill packs four different amphetamine salts into one tablet. What is its brand name?
Adderall: Drug mixture used mainly to treat ADHD and narcolepsy.
This Scottish physician shared the 1945 Nobel Prize for discovering penicillin, and in 1922 identified an enzyme in his own nasal discharge — who is he?
Alexander Fleming: Scottish physician and microbiologist (1881–1955)
This highly soluble, hygroscopic crystalline salt is prized as a high-nitrogen fertilizer but is also the major ingredient in the industrial explosive ANFO — what is it?
Ammonium nitrate: Chemical compound with formula NH4NO3.

Native to the Americas from northern Mexico to northern Argentina, this flowering plant genus is the largest in the arum family and includes types nicknamed flamingo flower and pigtail plant. What genus is it?
Anthurium: Genus of plants. Anthurium (Schott, 1829) is a genus of about 1,000 species of flowering plants, the largest genus of the arum family, Araceae.
These chitin-armored invertebrates must shed their exoskeletons to grow and circulate haemolymph through an open body cavity — and may number up to ten million species. What are they?
Arthropod: Phylum of invertebrates with jointed exoskeletons.

Flown by the Royal Air Force's Red Arrows display team, this British jet-powered advanced trainer has been license-built in India by Hindustan Aeronautics, with over 1,000 sold to 18 countries — which aircraft?
BAE Systems Hawk: Military training aircraft family.
Once chairman of the Nasdaq, this financier admitted to masterminding the largest-known Ponzi scheme in history, estimated at $65 billion — who is it?
Bernie Madoff: American financier and con artist (1938–2021)
Announced in 2011, this fourth-generation narrow-body jet introduced more efficient LEAP engines and split-tip winglets, with variants from the 7 up through the 10 — what aircraft is it?
Patented by Roche in 1961 and approved for medical use in 1974, which benzodiazepine, similar in effect to diazepam, is sometimes given as a presurgical sedative in 1.5, 3, or 6 mg tablets?
Bromazepam: Benzodiazepine drug. Bromazepam, sold under many brand names, is a benzodiazepine.
Designated Maryland's official state crustacean, this species is expected to benefit from climate change even as overfishing hurts other Chesapeake Bay fisheries — which species?
Callinectes sapidus: Species of crustacean. It is Maryland's largest commercial fishery and has been designated its state crustacean.
A wartime myth claimed eating this vegetable helped British pilots see in the dark — really a cover story for radar — which root vegetable?
Carrot: Root vegetable. The carrot (Daucus carota subsp. sativus) is a root vegetable in the umbellifer family Apiaceae.
Holder of 186 patents, this American engineer ran research at General Motors for nearly three decades and gave the world the electric car starter, leaded gasoline, and Freon — who was he?
Charles F. Kettering: American inventor, engineer and businessman (1876–1958)
Despite its common 'cat' nickname, this small nocturnal mammal from Africa and Asia is not a feline at all — and one African species yields a musky scent long used in perfumery — what is it?
Civet: Mammals of the families Viverridae and Nandiniidae and the genus Fossa.
Greenish-brown above and off-white below, this migratory leaf warbler is named onomatopoeically for its simple two-note song — which bird?
Common chiffchaff: Small migratory passerine bird found in Europe, Asia and north Africa.

This blood-feeding parasitic insect, scientifically Pthirus pubis, typically lives in coarse body hair and diverged from a gorilla-infecting relative about 3.3 million years ago — what is it commonly called?
Crab louse: Species of insect. The crab louse or pubic louse (Pthirus pubis) is an insect that is an obligate ectoparasite of humans, feeding exclusively on blood.
This Swedish tech entrepreneur founded and chairs a streaming giant, with a net worth estimated at $8.7 billion in December 2025 — who is he?
This bodily process breaks large food molecules into water-soluble components through both mechanical action like chewing and chemical action from enzymes — what's it called?
Digestion: Biological process of breaking down food.
Sometimes nicknamed 'math dyslexia' even though it's a distinct condition, this learning disorder involves persistent difficulty understanding numbers and performing calculations — what is it called?
This Italian-American physicist discovered two elements, technetium and astatine, plus the antiproton — the last earning him a share of the 1959 Nobel Prize in Physics. Who was he?
Emilio Segrè: Italian-American nuclear physicist and radiochemist (1905–1989)
Marketed under brand names like Arcoxia, this selective COX-2 inhibitor developed by Merck was approved in 63 countries by 2007 — everywhere, notably, except the United States — what is the drug?
This membranous bodily structure comes in superficial, visceral, and deep types, and a dangerous pressure buildup within it can cause compartment syndrome — what is it called?
Fascia: Layer of connective tissue in the body.
Sold under the brand name Luvox, this SSRI antidepressant treats OCD and other anxiety disorders, with milder side effects than most in its class except gastrointestinal ones — what drug is it?
Fluvoxamine: SSRI antidepressant. Fluvoxamine, sold under the brand name Luvox among others, is an antidepressant of the selective serotonin reuptake inhibitor (SSRI) class.
With a melting point of just under 30 degrees Celsius, this metal will turn to liquid in the palm of your hand — which element?
Gallium: Chemical element with atomic number 31 (Ga)
Found in birds, crocodilians, and earthworms alike, this thick-muscled digestive organ grinds food with the help of swallowed grit — what's it called?
Gizzard: Digestive organ of some animals.

Once classified as a subfamily of the seabasses, this diverse family of marine ray-finned fish is now treated as distinct, with most members drawn from two large genera. What are they commonly called?
Grouper: Family of fishes. The common name "grouper" is usually given to fish in one of two large genera: Epinephelus and Mycteroperca.
Nicknamed bindwood or lovestone, this clinging evergreen native to Europe scales tree trunks, walls, and fences — which plant?
Hedera helix: Species of flowering plant.
This genus of over 570 flowering plants — the only living genus in its family — includes the evergreen shrub famous for Christmas decorations and cards. What genus is it?
Holly: Genus of flowering plants. Ilex or holly is a genus of over 570 species of flowering plants in the family Aquifoliaceae, and the only living genus in that family.

This neurological disorder involves excessive sleepiness or time spent sleeping, sometimes linked to seasonal affective disorder, and appears under sleep-wake disorders in the DSM-5 — what is it called?

Hypersomnia: Neurological disorder of excessive time spent sleeping or excessive sleepiness. It can have many possible causes (such as seasonal affective disorder) and can cause distress and problems with functioning.
More than half of all animal species belong to this one chitinous-shelled group, each member sporting three body parts and three pairs of jointed legs — who are they?
Known as the 'snow monkey' for surviving areas buried in snow half the year, no other primate lives farther north than this species — which one?
Japanese macaque: Species of Old World monkey.
Also called the red date or Chinese date, this buckthorn-family fruit is eaten fresh, dried, or candied — what is it?
Jujube: Species of plant with edible fruit.
This colorless noble gas defined the length of the metre from 1960 to 1983, based on the wavelength of one of its spectral lines — which element?
Krypton: Chemical element with atomic number 36 (Kr)
This Turing Award winner brought order to the chaos of distributed computing — and, on the side, created the document-preparation system LaTeX and wrote its first manual. Who is he?
Leslie Lamport: American computer scientist and mathematician (born 1941)
Normally solitary and harmless, these short-horned grasshoppers can undergo a serotonin-triggered shift into gregarious swarming behavior under drought-then-growth conditions — what are they called?
Locust: Grasshopper that has a swarming phase.
Also called the dorado or common dolphinfish, this surface-dwelling ray-finned fish is found around the Gulf of Mexico, Costa Rica, and Hawaii — what is it?
Mahi-mahi: Species of fish. It is also widely called dorado (not to be confused with Salminus brasiliensis, a freshwater fish) and dolphin (not to be confused with the aquatic mammal dolphin).

Belonging to the ancient order Ephemeroptera and keeping primitive traits like long tails and wings that won't fold flat, which aquatic insect's water-dwelling nymphs signal a clean, unpolluted stream?
Mayfly: Aquatic insects of the order Ephemeroptera. Over 3,000 species of mayfly are known worldwide, grouped into over 400 genera in 42 families.
This colorless gas, made by swapping one hydrogen atom in ammonia for a methyl group, has a strong rotten-fish smell and serves as a building block for many compounds — what is it?
Famous for mimicking the songs of other birds — and even singing well past midnight — this bird can recognize individual humans and is the state bird of five U.S. states. What kind of bird is it?
Mockingbird: Family of birds. The only mockingbird commonly found in North America is the northern mockingbird.
This autoimmune disease attacks acetylcholine receptors at the neuromuscular junction, often causing drooping eyelids, double vision, and difficulty swallowing — which condition?
Myasthenia gravis: Autoimmune disease resulting in skeletal muscle weakness.
This semiaquatic salamander's juvenile phase is nicknamed an 'eft,' and adults return to the water every year to breed after living mostly on land — what is it?
Newt: Salamander in the subfamily Pleurodelinae.
Weighing up to 1,000 kg and resembling a fish head without a tail, this giant marine creature can be as tall as it is long when its fins are extended — what is it?
Ocean sunfish: Species of fish. The ocean sunfish (Mola mola), also known as the common mola, is one of the largest bony fish in the world.
This paired female gonad releases egg cells and secretes hormones that regulate the menstrual cycle and fertility — which organ?
Ovary: Female reproductive organ that produces egg cells.
He earned a PhD in physics from Cambridge for the first-ever thesis on quantum mechanics, then shared the 1933 Nobel Prize in Physics with Erwin Schrödinger — who is he?
First extracted from coal tar and now made from petroleum, this mildly acidic compound is a key precursor to Bakelite and nylon — what is it?
Widely planted along London's streets as a hybrid variety, this tree genus includes the sycamores of North America and can tower up to 50 meters — which genus?
Platanus: Genus of flowering plants constituting the family Platanaceae.

Arising over 60 million years ago from small tree-dwellers, this order favored big brains, binocular color vision and opposable thumbs to grasp among the branches — and it includes lemurs and apes — what is it?
Primate: Order of mammals. New primate species continue to be discovered: over 25 species were described in the 2000s, 36 in the 2010s, and six in the 2020s.

Known in France as the Patou and in the US by another name, this French livestock guardian breed hails from a range straddling France and Spain, protecting flocks from wolves and bears. What breed is it?
Pyrenean Mountain Dog: French breed of dog. The Pyrenean Mountain Dog (Chien de Montagne des Pyrénées) is a French breed of livestock guardian dog.

This Canadian-American inventor pulled off the first transmission of speech by radio in 1900 and the first two-way radiotelegraphy across the Atlantic in 1906, racking up hundreds of patents — seven granted after his death. Who was this AM-radio pioneer?
Reginald Fessenden: Canadian-American electrical engineer and inventor (1866–1932)
Commonly called the dog rose, this variable climbing wild plant is native to Europe, northwest Africa, and western Asia — which species?
Also known as mucopolysaccharidosis type III, this rare genetic disorder is caused by the body's inability to break down certain sugar molecules called glycosaminoglycans — what is it called?

Sanfilippo syndrome: Rare metabolism disorder. Sanfilippo syndrome, also known as mucopolysaccharidosis type III (MPS III), is a rare lifelong genetic disease that mainly affects the brain and spinal cord.
Serving as mayor of Moscow since 2010, this Russian politician previously headed the presidential administration and served as a deputy prime minister under Vladimir Putin — who is he?
Sergey Sobyanin: Mayor of Moscow since 2010. At the same time, Sobyanin was criticized for the banning of pride parades in the city, for which he was strongly condemned by LGBT groups.
Native to the Arctic tundra, this large white bird of prey is famous for being the only member of its family with predominantly pale plumage — which bird?
Snowy owl: Species of owl. The snowy owl (Bubo scandiacus), also known as the polar owl, the white owl and the Arctic owl, is a large, white owl of the true owl family.
This Polish-American mathematician on the Manhattan Project dreamed up the cellular automaton and the Monte Carlo method, and co-designed the thermonuclear bomb — who was he?
Stanisław Ulam: Polish mathematician and physicist (1909–1984)
Comprising around 90 species split between river martins and all other members, this family of aerial-feeding songbirds is thought to have evolved as hole-nesters in Africa — what are they called?
Swallow: Family of songbirds. The term "swallow" is used as the common name for Hirundo rustica in the United Kingdom and Ireland.
Made of collagen like its bone-to-bone cousin the ligament, this tough band of connective tissue instead links muscle to bone, and there are about 4,000 of them in your body — what is it called?
Tendon: Type of tissue that connects muscle to bone.
Native to Africa and the Middle East, this freshwater fish has become a global aquaculture staple but can turn invasive in warm habitats like Australia — which fish?
Tilapia: Common name for many species of fish.
Closely related to salmon, these carnivorous freshwater fish spawn in shallow gravel beds of headwater creeks after migrating upstream — what are they called?
Trout: Freshwater fish from subfamily Salmoninae.
Used to treat epilepsy and stabilize mood in bipolar disorder, this medication carries a serious risk of birth defects if taken during pregnancy — what is it?
Valproate: Medication used for epilepsy, bipolar disorder and migraine. Common side effects of valproate include nausea, vomiting, somnolence, and dry mouth.
Also known as ash pumpkin or winter melon, this South and Southeast Asian plant is grown for its very large fruit, eaten as a vegetable once mature — which plant?
Wax gourd: Species of vine and edible fruit.
Known to TV audiences as 'Dr. Now,' this Iranian-born American surgeon has spent over a decade helping patients on My 600-lb Life reach life-saving weight loss — who is he?
Younan Nowzaradan: Iranian-American surgeon, television personality, and author (born 1944)
Arsenic is denoted by which symbol?
The symbol for arsenic is As. Arsenic is a chemical element; it has the symbol As and atomic number 33.
What is the chemical symbol for nihonium?
The symbol for nihonium is Nh. Nihonium is a synthetic chemical element; it has symbol Nh and atomic number 113.

In what year was Jennifer Connelly born?
Jennifer Connelly: Jennifer Lynn Connelly (born December 12, 1970) is an American actress.
In what year was Phil Collins born?
Phil Collins: Philip David Charles Collins (born 30 January 1951) is an English singer, drummer, songwriter, record producer, and actor.
